items.name: Driver hours-of-service (HOS)
items.version: US: 49 CFR Part 395 (FMCSA); EU: Regulation (EC) No 561/2006
items.scope: Limits on commercial driver on-duty/driving time and mandatory rest breaks; typically enforced via an electronic logging device (ELD) in the US.
items.notes: Applies mainly to commercial motor vehicles above regulatory weight/passenger thresholds; exact thresholds and rest-break rules differ by jurisdiction and are flagged, not implemented, here. Neither cloned source (karrio, fleetbase) implements HOS logic; this entry is domain knowledge, not a claim that either product is compliant.

provenance.notes: fleetbase models driver time_window_start/end and schedule_constraints, which HOS compliance would build on, but does not implement HOS rules itself. Reasoned applicability.

items.name: Dangerous goods (hazmat) shipping
items.version: Road: ADR (UNECE); Air: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR)
items.jurisdiction: ADR: Europe (road); IATA DGR: global (air, contractual via carriers)
items.scope: Classification, labeling, packaging, and documentation requirements for shipments containing hazardous materials.
items.notes: Neither cloned source models a dangerous-goods classification field; flagged from the domain brief as a jurisdiction-specific concern for any product that ships or transports regulated materials, not verified against either implementation.

provenance.notes: karrio's Commodity/Parcel models carry declared value and content fields that a DG classification would extend; not itself evidence of DG support. Single source, reasoned.

items.name: Customs and import/export regulations
items.version: Varies by jurisdiction (e.g. US CBP, EU Union Customs Code)
items.jurisdiction: Destination and origin country of an international shipment
items.scope: Declaration of contents, value, and origin for cross-border shipments; duties and taxes calculation.
items.notes: Flagged per the brief's guidance that customs is jurisdiction-specific and requires human review; not a claim that any implementation is customs-compliant.

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.customs embedded field is the only direct evidence; single source, no specific jurisdiction's rules verified.
